system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
*Buyer-side assessment based on the Seller’s update and disclosure letter only; the complete SPA and underlying DD records should be checked before agreeing drafting.*

| Issue | Seller’s position | What Buyer should want | Recommendation and one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001: General liability cap** | General Warranty Claims capped at **20% of price (AUD 4.8m)**; Seller says positions are final. | A materially higher cap, with separate higher or uncapped treatment for specified risks; no assumption that the preamble establishes an agreed bargain. | **Reopen; seek a higher cap and risk-specific carve-outs.** A AUD 4.8m ceiling may not cover material warranty losses in a AUD 24m acquisition. |
| **SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket** | AUD 25,000 de minimis; AUD 250,000 tipping threshold, but only the excess is recoverable (deductible basket). | A lower per-claim threshold and a tipping basket, so once crossed all qualifying losses are recoverable; clarify aggregation and related claims. | **Reject the deductible basket; propose tipping treatment and sensible aggregation.** Deductible treatment leaves Buyer bearing the first AUD 250,000 even after the basket is crossed. |
| **SPA-N-003: General claims time limit** | Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion; Seller proposes applying any limitation to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise. | A longer period for general warranties and express, separate periods for tax, fundamental, specific indemnity and other claims; preserve claims notified in time through resolution. | **Amend to separate claim-specific periods.** A blanket default risks cutting off claims whose nature or agreed protection warrants longer survival. |
| **SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title warranties subject to the general cap and time limits. | Separate, substantially higher or uncapped cap and longer limitation period for title and capacity; specific protection for valid ownership and transfer of all shares. | **Reject same-regime treatment.** A general cap and 18-month limit inadequately protect the core bargain of acquiring 100% of the shares. |
| **SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims; no express fraud carve-out is stated. | Expressly exclude fraud and fraudulent misrepresentation (including as legally appropriate, the relevant party’s own conduct) from caps, thresholds, time bars, exclusive remedy and non-reliance protections, subject to applicable law. | **Add an express fraud carve-out.** The draft should not purport to shield fraud through general limitations or remedy language. |
| **SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope** | General disclosure of the entire indexed data room as at a stated time, plus accounts, statutory registers and public corporate records; specific disclosures also provided. | Require fair, specific, sufficiently detailed disclosures against the relevant warranties; exclude blanket data-room/public-register disclosure or limit it to clearly identified, accessible documents. | **Reject blanket general disclosure; retain only properly particularised disclosures.** Sweeping disclosure can neutralise warranties without identifying what risk is being disclosed. |
| **SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for matters known to Buyer or its advisers, including matters discoverable in the data room or public records. | No broad constructive-knowledge bar; at most, narrowly defined actual knowledge of named individuals, with no impact on fraud, specific indemnities or matters fairly disclosed under agreed rules. | **Delete or tightly narrow the qualifier.** “Discoverable” knowledge improperly shifts diligence risk to Buyer and makes ordinary access a defence to claims. |
| **SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent** | Seller to use reasonable endeavours; consent treated as satisfied on delivery of written consent. DD-002 shows ~AUD 3.6m FY26 revenue (~30%); final consent and satisfaction of clause 11.3 conditions are absent. | Completion conditional on obtaining effective consent and satisfying applicable conditions, with evidence, no adverse variation, and a walk-away or other agreed protection if not obtained. | **Make this a genuine condition precedent, not deemed satisfied on receipt alone.** Bluefen is a major revenue source and the disclosed conditions remain unverified. |
| **SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility** | Approximately AUD 3.2m outstanding; release to follow Completion. Disclosure confirms it is not repaid and no final discharge is included. | Repayment at or before Completion from agreed funds flow, with lender payoff evidence, release/discharge of all security and any required termination of facilities as completion deliverables. | **Require simultaneous repayment and effective releases at Completion.** A post-Completion promise leaves Buyer exposed to debt and encumbered assets. |
| **SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses** | AUD 420,000 conditional Completion bonuses are omitted from draft funds flow; payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs are not addressed. Seller calls them its matter. | Identify and allocate the full cost, including on-costs; include it in the funds flow and debt/expense or price mechanics as appropriate, with no duplicate recovery and clear responsibility for payment and payroll compliance. | **Resolve and fund the full liability in the SPA and funds flow before signing.** The disclosed bonuses are conditional on Completion and currently omitted, with potential additional costs unquantified. |
| **SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity** | Existing indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; DD-004 requires cleared payment of every SOW3 fee before transfer of Project Materials; DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open, with no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment. | A specific indemnity and completion protection covering payment, transfer/assignment, ownership, access and usable rights in all relevant materials, plus remediation or price protection if transfer fails. | **Expand the indemnity and make rights transfer a deliverable.** The disclosed payment condition and missing assignment evidence create a direct risk to acquired IP. |
| **SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident** | Seller characterises DD-006 as preliminary and not expected to be material; disclosure says an unintended external link may contain ~1,240 records, with access, scope and notification status unresolved. | Specific incident warranties/indemnity or other tailored protection; complete investigation, preserve evidence, make legally required notifications, deliver findings, and allocate remediation costs and liabilities. | **Treat as an unresolved specific risk, not dismiss it as immaterial.** The record set and potential exposure are not yet established, so targeted protections and investigation are needed. |
| **SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals** | Three renewals total AUD 330,000, described as ordinary-course costs; disclosure does not establish whether they are terminable, accrued or unavoidable. | Confirm contract terms, timing, termination rights and any committed or accrued amounts; reflect liabilities in completion accounts/debt-like items or specific protections as appropriate. | **Do not accept the “ordinary course” label without verification and price-mechanics treatment.** The disclosure does not establish whether the renewals create binding post-Completion obligations. |
| **SPA-N-014: Category separation** | Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims; Seller proposes the same limits for claims unless expressly stated otherwise. | Clearly separate general warranties, fundamental/title, tax, specific indemnities, covenant/contract claims, fraud and other claims, with expressly tailored caps, baskets, periods and remedies. | **Require an express claim-category architecture.** A one-size-fits-all regime can unintentionally restrict protections that should operate separately. |
| **SPA-N-015: Title verification** | Relies on DD-012 share register showing Seller as holder of 100% of issued shares. | Verify the register and corporate records, confirm fully paid shares and absence of options, encumbrances or competing rights, and obtain executed transfers and required corporate deliverables at Completion. | **Treat the register as evidence, not conclusive verification.** The disclosure itself says Buyer has not completed its own verification. |
| **SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms** | Seller says tax and IP positions are settled under the general regime; no separate tax or broader IP terms are set out here. | Review the complete SPA and DD; negotiate tailored tax warranties/indemnity and IP ownership, infringement, licensing and chain-of-title protections, with appropriate caps and survival periods distinct from general warranties. | **Keep both open pending review and negotiate them expressly.** The Seller’s summary does not establish the scope or adequacy of the operative protections. |
=== END ADVICE ===
